advisor_identified: William D. Irvine, York University historian of modern France and Italy, teaching there from 1971 to 2011.

doctorate.title: The Republican Federation of France during the 1930's

evidence.says: Princeton University Library attributes The Republican Federation of France during the 1930's to William D. Irvine, dates it 1972, and explicitly records it as a PhD thesis at Princeton University, 1972.
Princeton Alumni Weekly identifies William D. Irvine as a York University historian teaching from 1971 to 2011 and states that he earned his PhD in history from Princeton in 1972.

York identifies William D. Irvine as its professor emeritus, a graduate and undergraduate teacher of modern French and Italian history from 1971 to 2011. It confirms a Princeton PhD but gives the year as 1971.
York faculty profile lists William D. Irvine as professor emeritus in the Department of History, with research interests in modern France and Italy.

notes: The linked dissertation matches the Princeton catalogue in author, institution, year and exact title. The doctorate year is reported inconsistently: York says 1971, whereas Princeton Alumni Weekly and the Princeton thesis catalogue say 1972. The latter date is used here; the discrepancy does not indicate a namesake.
